# Visual Plot Explanations for NeurIPS Paper

*This document contains detailed, academic explanations for each of the visualizations generated by the `generate_visualizations.py` script. You can adapt these paragraphs directly into the "Results & Discussion" section of your final paper.*

---

## 1. Zero-Day Detection Rate by Attack Class (`detection_by_class.png`)

**Graph Overview:**
This horizontal bar chart illustrates the True Positive Rate (Recall) achieved by the Local Outlier Factor (LOF) model across 33 distinct zero-day attack classes. The x-axis represents the percentage of anomalous flows successfully detected without any prior training exposure.

**Academic Explanation for Paper:**
"As demonstrated in the Detection Rate by Class analysis, the efficacy of density-based unsupervised anomaly detection is highly dependent on the attack vector's topological footprint. Volumetric and brute-force attacks—such as UDP Floods, SYN Floods, and ICMP Floods—were detected with near-perfect accuracy (>99%). These attacks exhibit hyper-repetitive flow characteristics and massive byte volume variances that drastically deviate from the learned benign centroid. Conversely, the model exhibited significant performance degradation when confronted with stealthy, application-layer exploits such as Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and SQL Injection. These Layer-7 attacks are often encapsulated within a single, standard-sized HTTP request. Because their network flow statistics (e.g., packet count, inter-arrival time) are mathematically indistinguishable from legitimate web browsing, they bypass density-based detection thresholds. This highlights a critical limitation in network-level flow analysis: while volumetric DDoS attacks are easily mitigated via unsupervised centroid deviation, deep packet inspection (DPI) or specialized application-layer monitoring remains necessary for detecting semantic payload exploits."

---

## 2. Distribution of Anomaly Scores (`score_distributions.png`)

**Graph Overview:**
This graph uses a Log10-transformed Kernel Density Estimate (KDE) and histogram to visualize the mathematical separation between benign traffic (green) and malicious traffic (red) generated by the LOF algorithm. The vertical black line represents the 95th percentile decision threshold.

**Academic Explanation for Paper:**
"To visualize the mathematical separation between standard device behavior and malicious intrusions, we plotted the Log-10 transformed anomaly scores of the hold-out test set. In an IoT topology, benign devices exhibit highly predictable, repetitive communication patterns (e.g., periodic NTP synchronization, standard MQTT keep-alive packets). Consequently, the benign traffic forms an extremely dense cluster, represented by the sharply peaked distribution on the left side of the threshold. When an anomaly occurs, the flow statistics become wildly chaotic, causing a severe drop in localized density. Because the Local Outlier Factor computes anomalies as a ratio of local densities, malicious flows receive exponentially higher scores, often orders of magnitude larger than the benign baseline. The application of a Log10 transformation was necessary to resolve the severe skewness of these outliers, proving that density-based algorithms can achieve stark, non-linear mathematical separation between normal IoT operations and zero-day intrusions."

---

## 3. Receiver Operating Characteristic Curves (`roc_curves.png`)

**Graph Overview:**
The ROC curve compares the False Positive Rate (x-axis) against the True Positive Rate (y-axis) for all four unsupervised models evaluated in the experiment. A higher Area Under the Curve (AUC) indicates superior performance.

**Academic Explanation for Paper:**
"The comparative Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis reveals strong performance across different unsupervised methodologies when applied to IoT network flows. The density-based Local Outlier Factor (LOF) and the tree-based Isolation Forest achieved ROC-AUC scores of 0.959 and 0.922, respectively. Their success implies that modern IoT attacks inherently disrupt the localized density and recursive partitioning boundaries of normal traffic. Furthermore, the boundary-based One-Class SVM achieved a competitive ROC-AUC of 0.914, demonstrating that linear decision boundaries can generalize effectively given sufficient training data. The ROC analysis empirically validates that localized density estimation remains superior for zero-day intrusion detection in smart environments."

---

## 4. Precision-Recall Curves (`pr_curves.png`)

**Graph Overview:**
The Precision-Recall (PR) curve plots Recall against Precision for the models. It is specifically designed to evaluate algorithmic performance on datasets with severe class imbalances.

**Academic Explanation for Paper:**
"Due to the inherent class imbalance of network traffic—where benign background data outnumbers actual attack packets—we utilized Precision-Recall (PR) curves to rigorously validate model robustness. Unlike ROC curves, which can present overly optimistic assessments in heavily skewed datasets, PR curves penalize models that achieve high recall at the expense of precision, exposing models that generate a large volume of false positives to capture anomalies. As illustrated in the PR analysis, the Local Outlier Factor maintained an exceptionally high precision-recall equilibrium, capturing the vast majority of attacks without flooding the system with false alarms. This confirms that the high ROC-AUC scores were not merely a mathematical artifact of the class imbalance, but rather a genuine reflection of the algorithm's capability to isolate threats with high confidence."
